title.narrative: The 3Rs phase II for Resilience (Retention, Recharge, Reuse) project

description.narrative:
Jordan faces one of the most severe water crises globally, driven by extreme water scarcity, climate variability, groundwater over-abstraction, land degradation, and increasing exposure to floods and droughts. These challenges are particularly evident in the Azraq, Amman–Zarqa, Yarmouk, and Northern Jordan Valley basins, where declining groundwater levels, unpredictable rainfall, and recurring flash floods threaten livelihoods, infrastructure, and ecosystems. In northern and eastern governorates—including Irbid, Mafraq, Zarqa, Balqa, Ajloun, Jerash, and eastern Amman—these pressures are further compounded in areas hosting refugees and vulnerable communities.
The 3Rs for Resilience (Retention, Recharge, Reuse) project responds to these interconnected challenges by scaling climate-smart water management solutions that strengthen water security, reduce climate risks, and enhance institutional resilience. The project builds on the achievements and lessons of the first 3Rs phase (2021–2025), funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, which demonstrated the effectiveness of water harvesting interventions in reducing flood impacts, improving groundwater recharge, restoring degraded landscapes, and supporting agricultural livelihoods. Phase 1 also generated valuable technical knowledge, datasets, and institutional partnerships, while initiating national policy dialogue on water harvesting.
Building on this foundation, the new project represents a shift from pilot interventions to basin-level impact. It focuses on vulnerable areas across four priority hydrological basins—Yarmouk, Amman–Zarqa, Azraq, and the Northern Jordan Valley—where water scarcity, groundwater depletion, flood risk, and ecosystem degradation intersect.
At its core, the project applies the Retention–Recharge–Reuse (3Rs) approach to increase decentralized water availability while reducing flood risks. Interventions combine upstream watershed management, climate-smart water harvesting, and managed aquifer recharge with urban and peri-urban measures such as rooftop water harvesting, localized stormwater retention, and improved flood risk management. Digital monitoring platforms, early warning systems, and decision-support tools will strengthen municipal preparedness and data-driven water management.
The project also strengthens institutional capacity through applied training, basin planning support, and national knowledge systems, ensuring long-term sustainability and integration within Jordan’s water governance frameworks. By improving water access, restoring ecosystems, and strengthening resilience, the project benefits vulnerable communities—including women, youth, and refugee-hosting populations—while contributing to Jordan’s National Water Strategy 2023–2040 and the Netherlands’ priorities on water security, climate resilience, and inclusive development.
